Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(6,-6).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(6,-6),$ we can substitute $x=6$ and $y=-6$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}6=2pt \\ -6=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2pt \\ 3 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 & =p{(\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ -6 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ -6 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(-\frac{3}{2})t,\,y=(-\frac{3}{2}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=-3t,\,y=-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}.
$$
